Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)
Manifold Model Falling-MAP Initial Duration (TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Normally leave alone. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used instead of the other Map A tables while the car is at a standstill under high load (speed 5 km/h or less, pedal 80 % or more, load 40 % or more, for 1 s). Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while an unidentified speed/pedal/load flag is set. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): an amount added to the estimate at the start of each fuel cut, by air quantity, which then decays away by Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): how fast the fuel-cut term from Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step decays, by air quantity (1.0 = no decay).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (2D)
table.description: Later-software version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C9878): added to S = Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) 064D64 x Retard Multiplier A (Enriched) 064E78 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 008D6C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80: added to U = Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) 064E04 x Retard Multiplier B (Enriched) 064E54 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 008E0C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to the second exhaust temperature estimate while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0) and FFF8AE27 bit 4 is clear. 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D8F60 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C965C): added to Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Enriched) 064A0C x Retard Multiplier 064AAC / 256. LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 008A64. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. This, not 1B, sets wide-open-throttle intake timing near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle), at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. Near sea level Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. This is the table that sets light-load intake timing on most cars.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to the final intake cam target near sea level (whatever the TGV state; with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)

At light part throttle the TGVs close and Exhaust Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = more overlap. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. Higher = more overlap. High-pedal meaning inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap (internal EGR).

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset A (Altitude)

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target near sea level, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. It applies whatever the TGV state: with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3. Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B is added on top of it in all TGV states, so with the TGVs closed both act.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 024AF0 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 02BE84. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C760 by the code that reads it (read). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00B50C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set, on automatic/CVT cars.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear, which happens only with the AT/CVT coding (AT state FFF8A7DD 0 or 5; 0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C754 by the code that reads it (read). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00B500. Confidence: read.

Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:
Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart, by start type and coolant. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). TGVs not forced closed. Selected instead of the cranking value only inside the engine stop-start restart window (FFF89053 bit3/bit4 with the FFF88ADA bit3 edge, before the decay delay), by start type FFF8A6E8 (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C5E8 by the code that reads it (read). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00B36C. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). TGV Coolant Minimum
table.description: Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions).

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter)
table.description: Air flow below which the TGVs may close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions together with torque and coolant). Raise it (with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)) to let the TGVs close at higher air flow; once closed they reopen above the Exit value.

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)
table.description: Air flow above which a TGV-close request clears again (probably reopening the TGVs); the upper end of the hysteresis with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter). Keep it above the Enter value.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 037A46 by the code that reads it (read). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Address 040942. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum.
Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182B28 (read, all stack args checked in the assembly) has three sources for the booster vacuum Confidence: read.

table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Same data block as descriptor 05D468 (one entry). Road speed per 1000 rpm for gear index 1-8. 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.3 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 6 steps here, 11.0 to 53.9 over 8 in the Alternate table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D4D8 by the code that reads it (read). LF9C200B: same code as LF9C100P; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00C380. Confidence: inferred.

LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Trigger A)
table.description: Extra fuel added while the knock torque cap's trigger a trigger is set, by engine speed and load; it fades out afterwards.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Trigger B)
table.description: Extra fuel added while the knock torque cap's trigger b trigger is set, by engine speed and load; it fades out afterwards.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Margin)

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment Decay

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment Ramp (Margin)
table.description: How fast the margin-trigger knock event enrichment moves toward its target and back, per pass, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)

Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009870. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009610. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0091B4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A818 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0091C8. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00932C. Confidence: inferred.

Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st)
table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AF94 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2

table.description: AT/CVT version of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed)
table.description: Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)
table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Closed)
table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Normal)

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Correction to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal), the second pulse; positive = later. Edit with that table.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal pressed or the car moving.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle, Alternate)
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection).

Purge Valve Duty
table.description: Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.

table.name: Ignition Dwell Time
table.description: Coil charge (dwell) time in milliseconds by rpm and battery voltage, used whenever the engine runs. More dwell gives a stronger spark but heats the coils.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open)
Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Closed)
Timing Request Enrichment Retard
table.description: Retard ramped into the timing request while open-loop power enrichment is active, by load and rpm. The ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and request + knock advance.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (Alternate, Below 5000 RPM)
Base Timing Coolant Compensation (Alternate, Above 5000 RPM)

Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Closed)
Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Open)
Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Closed)
Knock Event Detector: Low Timing
table.description: Watches for ignition timing pulled down to a floor that depends on DAM; when it trips, the knock-event torque limit applies.

table.name: Knock Event Detector: Knocking Cylinders
table.description: Counts cylinders whose knock signal is above the knock threshold while knock correction is already deep; when the count runs up, the knock-event torque limit applies until the learned values are reset.

table.name: Knock Event Latch
table.description: Keeps the knock-event torque limit on after a trip, across key cycles, until the learned knock values are reset.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Passes
table.description: Consecutive passes the timing must stay at or below the floor before the low-timing detector trips.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Hysteresis
table.description: Once the timing is at the floor, it must rise this far above it to count as recovered.

table.name: Knock Event Cylinder Count Limit (Feedback)
table.description: Knocking cylinders, summed while feedback knock correction is at or below its threshold, that trip the detector.

table.name: Knock Event Feedback Correction Threshold
table.description: Knocking cylinders are summed while feedback knock correction is at or below this.

table.name: Knock Event Feedback Correction Hysteresis
table.description: Once summing, feedback knock correction must recover this far above the threshold to stop.

table.name: Knock Event Cylinder Count Limit (Fine Learning)
table.description: Knocking cylinders, summed while fine learning knock correction is at or below its threshold, that trip the detector.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Threshold
table.description: Knocking cylinders are summed while fine learning knock correction is at or below this.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Hysteresis
table.description: Once summing, fine learning knock correction must recover this far above the threshold to stop.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Floor
table.description: Ignition timing floor of the low-timing detector at the lowest DAM factor.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Floor (DAM Adder)
table.description: Added to the low-timing floor in proportion to Knock Event Low Timing DAM Factor.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing DAM Factor
table.description: How much of the DAM adder applies, by DAM (128 = all of it).

table.name: Knock Torque Cap: Margin Trigger
table.description: Switches on the margin trigger of the knock torque cap: when the knock margin index falls to Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold, the torque ceiling ramps down to the Margin curve.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap: Coolant Condition Bypass
table.description: With this set, the margin trigger also works below Knock Torque Cap Coolant Minimum (unless an ECU flag blocks it).

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold
table.description: Knock margin index at or below which the margin trigger of the knock torque cap sets, by engine speed and load. Lower values let the engine run with less margin before the cap comes in.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Margin Hysteresis
table.description: Once the margin trigger is set, the threshold is raised by this much, so the margin index must climb clearly above it before the trigger releases.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Coolant Minimum
table.description: Coolant temperature from which the margin trigger works without the bypass.

table.name: Knock Margin Base
table.description: Starting value of the knock margin index by engine speed and load. The index is this, less intake air temperature 2 in degrees C, plus the spark and A/F terms; the knock torque cap's margin trigger sets when it falls to Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold. Lower values bring the cap and the margin enrichment in sooner.

table.name: Knock Margin Spark Weight
table.description: How strongly Knock Margin Spark Factor moves the knock margin index, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Margin Spark Factor
table.description: Knock margin term by how far the primary ignition request sits above the ignition timing ceiling; 50 is neutral, lower values take margin away. Scaled by Knock Margin Spark Weight.

table.name: Knock Margin A/F Weight
table.description: How strongly Knock Margin A/F Factor moves the knock margin index, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Margin A/F Factor
table.description: Knock margin term by the measured air/fuel ratio; 50 is neutral and higher values add margin. Scaled by Knock Margin A/F Weight.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0); this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 6)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires (variant with an extra internal condition set).
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 6. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00B07C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00A360. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted DAM/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B560 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00A374. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)

Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 4, Short Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 4 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 4 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 8)
table.description:
Knock-detection background step for event slot 1, frequency channel 8.
Details: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 8 of 8 (index 7 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 7 of cal 0x1B97C is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_7 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C180[7] when FFF8A7C2 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D01C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00C078. Confidence: inferred.

Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AF1C > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA6C, read). FFF8AE5E counts 10 ms passes while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 > cal 0x229E6 (0; hysteresis 0x229E8) (0x0BA48C, read). FFF8AE64 counts passes while the pedal-released flag FFF88C64 bit 5 is set and speed <= cal 0x229EC (0; hysteresis 0x229EE) (0x0BA7E0, read); FFF8AF1C counts passes while speed <= cal 0x22A0E (0; hysteresis 0x22A10) (0x0C065C, read). So they are the time stopped (pedal released / any pedal) since the car last moved. FFF88BAA is a byte copied from FFF8CC56 / FFF8CC01 / FFF8CC3B (0x080000 segment); its meaning is not identified, so the axis is raw. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Margin)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its margin trigger is set and the selector flag is clear, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Margin, Selector)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its margin trigger is set and the selector flag is set, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger A)

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger A, Selector)

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger B)

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger B, Selector)

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 Reset MAP

table.description: Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables).

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit (AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit Hysteresis (AT/CVT)
table.description: How far below the Park/Neutral RPM Limit the engine has to fall before the cut ends.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed

Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal)
table.description: The speed limiter in use: the share of the driver's pedal request allowed (100 % = no limit) by vehicle speed. It works above Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Minimum RPM. The other three speed tables are variants for drive mode 3 (Intelligent) and for a VDC flag: to move or remove the limit, edit all four, or turn on Pedal Limits Disable. The fuel-cut Vehicle Speed Limit set is a separate limiter.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Minimum RPM
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: Takes over from the speed tables when the vehicle speed cannot be trusted (a speed sensor fault, or CAN messages from the transmission or VDC missing): the pedal request is then limited by engine speed. Leave it as it is unless you know you need to change it.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description: Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (Alt)
table.description: The live version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter on 2017+ ROMs.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter used while the TGVs are closed. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.description: The live version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed) on 2017+ ROMs.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter Baro Factor

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
