table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
Details: When used: whenever FFF88ADA bit 7 (manual-transmission coding) is clear, i.e. on the AT/CVT coding. The A/B weight FFF8AE26 (0x0B9C78) starts at 0 and its step cals 0x22FBE/0x22FC0 are 0, so it stays 0 and the output is this table alone; the matching non-AT/CVT table is then ignored (read). FFF88ADA bit 7 is set on the manual coding, so this table is unused on manual cars. Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB670, read): FFF8AEB4 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB4; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table B of map set 2 = Drive Mode 1, Default (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions: mode 4 = Sport Sharp, mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive). KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description:
Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.
Details: When used: Monitor copy; keep identical. Byte-for-byte copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT) (data and axes) in separate storage, read by a second module (0x1873C4/0x1874BC/0x1875BC/0x1876BC, rpm x FFF88FE2, same A-then-B lookup order and weight structure, into FFF8BBAE/BBB2/BBB6/BBBA). Almost certainly the electronic-throttle torque monitor: change it together with the primary map or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Drive mode 2: SI-Drive Sport (S). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
Details: When used: whenever FFF88ADA bit 7 (manual-transmission coding) is clear, i.e. on the AT/CVT coding. The A/B weight FFF8AE26 (0x0B9C78) starts at 0 and its step cals 0x22FBE/0x22FC0 are 0, so it stays 0 and the output is this table alone; the matching non-AT/CVT table is then ignored (read). FFF88ADA bit 7 is set on the manual coding, so this table is unused on manual cars. Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB770, read): FFF8AEB8 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB8; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table B of map set 3 = Drive Mode 2 (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions: mode 4 = Sport Sharp, mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive). KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description:
Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.
Details: When used: Monitor copy; keep identical. Byte-for-byte copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT) (data and axes) in separate storage, read by a second module (0x1873C4/0x1874BC/0x1875BC/0x1876BC, rpm x FFF88FE2, same A-then-B lookup order and weight structure, into FFF8BBAE/BBB2/BBB6/BBBA). Almost certainly the electronic-throttle torque monitor: change it together with the primary map or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding. AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5). Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 with FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5). Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F714. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit (AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.
Details: u16 rpm x 0.1953125. Latch FFF8A63B bit 0 (0x0C07F8): set while FFF8A63B bit 1 and rpm FFF8CE9C >= this; held down to this - the hysteresis. FFF8A63B bit 1 (0x0C0850): P/N switch FFF88ADA bit 6 (or fault flag FFF88E2B bit 2), manual coding FFF88ADA bit 7 clear, TCM range code FFF8A8DC 5 or 7 (or TCM-data fault flag FFF88E2B bit 1). The latch lets the cut level FFF8A64F through to the cylinder-cut thresholds in 0x0C1AC8, as the limit states do. Addresses are LF75404S. (read; that range codes 5 and 7 are P and N is inferred: the switch input must agree) Confidence: read.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit Hysteresis (AT/CVT)
table.description:
How far below the Park/Neutral RPM Limit the engine has to fall before the cut ends.
Details: u16 rpm x 0.1953125, subtracted from the limit while the latch FFF8A63B bit 0 is set (0x0C07F8, saturating at 0). (read) Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding, while the in-Drive idle condition FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant): automatic coding, neutral input clear, pedal released, slow) and afterwards until the in-Drive idle air reduction FFF8B160 has ramped back to its target. Never on a manual car (inferred from that chain). 0x0F2248 (read): when FFF8A7E4 bit 4 is set, B242 = this(coolant) << 6 (12.5 rpm per count) replaces the idle-mode target chain. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 2 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description:
Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only while FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (0x0F38D0, read): automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear) and the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 clear, accelerator released, speed FFF99835 within cals 0x2583F..0x25841, rpm below cal 0x25842 and below @025886(coolant), no speed-sensor/CAN faults; so never on a manual car (read). 0x0EAA40 (read): FFF8B162 = this(coolant) + Idle Air Reduction In Drive (RPM Error)(rpm - target rpm FFF8B236, coolant) + a ramp term (cals 0x25838..0x2583C), >= 0, capped by @025846(coolant); FFF8B160 follows it at cal 0x25834/0x25836 (86) per pass and is subtracted at half weight from the idle air FFF8B200 (0x0F0AF8, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description:
Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant) (automatic coding only). 0x0EAA40 (read): added to the coolant term with the rpm error FFF8CE9C - FFF8B236 (s16, rpm x 5.12) and coolant FFF88A44 as axes. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.
Details: 0x0ECA08 (read; call 0x0ECA88/0x0ECA94 R5 checked): while FFF88A26 bit0 (idle, inferred), engine running (FFF88A27 bit0 clear) and FFF99835 below cal 0x259C8 (255, i.e. always), B1AE = this(new target - ramped target = B236 - B23C/4, capped at cal 0x259CA = 1000 rpm); B1AE enters the idle air at half weight. A positive step (target raised) adds air ahead of the ramp. Used when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear (bit0 = FFF8A7DD in 1..4 or 6, 0x0F38B0). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, standstill in gear. Input FFF88A44 (coolant, read in the disassembly by the same R5). 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, in neutral/park. Input FFF88A44 (coolant). 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (AT/CVT)
table.description:

Details: When used: AT/CVT codings only, while FFF8A618 bit 0 is clear. Same role as Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (0x0F6D98, read). Selection: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain is used while FFF8A618 bit 0 is set, which is always on the manual coding (cal 0x2F794 bit 1 clear, 0x0B8544, read); the (AT/CVT) table is used on AT/CVT codings while FFF8A618 bit 0 is clear (FFF886B0 bit 6 set after the first cal 0x34978 passes, not identified); the table when the manual flag FFF886AB bit 7 is set and either bit 0 is clear or cal 0x2F794 bit 2 is clear (rule: (A618 b0 = 0 or (0x2F794 b2 = 0 and 886AB b7)) ?: this one, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (MT Coding)
table.description:

Selection: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain is used while FFF8A618 bit 0 is set, which is always on the manual coding (cal 0x2F794 bit 1 clear, 0x0B8544, read); the (AT/CVT) table is used on AT/CVT codings while FFF8A618 bit 0 is clear (FFF886B0 bit 6 set after the first cal 0x34978 passes, not identified); the table when the manual flag FFF886AB bit 7 is set and either bit 0 is clear or cal 0x2F794 bit 2 is clear (rule: (A618 b0 = 0 or (0x2F794 b2 = 0 and 886AB b7)) ?: this one, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1).
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the AT/CVT curve branch, mirrored by the MT branch that reads Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1); the MT coding flag s4 picks the MT curve). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. Confidence: read.

Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 5 (0x0DBB20, read). Phase factor (x/255) by the rpm swing count FFF8A75E. With gear FFF88FCE = 0 or above 6 no table is read and the last factor is held (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. Confidence: inferred.

AT version of Closed-Pedal Timing Target, used with the pedal released while the transmission is probably in a drive range.
Details: When used: only with the automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear), while the debounced range state FFF8A7D9 (0x0EA0E0 from FFF8CE63, which 0x06B68C builds from the discrete inputs FFF8A2A1) is 1 or 2 (in a drive range, inferred). Never on a manual car (read). Same role as Closed-Pedal Timing Target. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description:
AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear (never on the manual coding), FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
Details: When used: whenever FFF88ADA bit 7 (manual-transmission coding) is clear, i.e. on the AT/CVT coding. The A/B weight FFF8AE26 (0x0B9C78) starts at 0 and its step cals 0x22FBE/0x22FC0 are 0, so it stays 0 and the output is this table alone; the matching non-AT/CVT table is then ignored (read). FFF88ADA bit 7 is set on the manual coding, so this table is unused on manual cars. Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB670, read): FFF8AEB4 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB4; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table B of map set 2 = Drive Mode 1, Default (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions: mode 4 = Sport Sharp, mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive). KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description:
Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.
Details: When used: Monitor copy; keep identical. Byte-for-byte copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT) (data and axes) in separate storage, read by a second module (0x1873C4/0x1874BC/0x1875BC/0x1876BC, rpm x FFF88FE2, same A-then-B lookup order and weight structure, into FFF8BBAE/BBB2/BBB6/BBBA). Almost certainly the electronic-throttle torque monitor: change it together with the primary map or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:

(1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 with FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit (AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.
Details: u16 rpm x 0.1953125. Latch FFF8A63B bit 0 (0x0C07F8): set while FFF8A63B bit 1 and rpm FFF8CE9C >= this; held down to this - the hysteresis. FFF8A63B bit 1 (0x0C0850): P/N switch FFF88ADA bit 6 (or fault flag FFF88E2B bit 2), manual coding FFF88ADA bit 7 clear, TCM range code FFF8A8DC 5 or 7 (or TCM-data fault flag FFF88E2B bit 1). The latch lets the cut level FFF8A64F through to the cylinder-cut thresholds in 0x0C1AC8, as the limit states do. Addresses are LF75404S. (read; that range codes 5 and 7 are P and N is inferred: the switch input must agree) Confidence: read.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit Hysteresis (AT/CVT)
table.description:
How far below the Park/Neutral RPM Limit the engine has to fall before the cut ends.
Details: u16 rpm x 0.1953125, subtracted from the limit while the latch FFF8A63B bit 0 is set (0x0C07F8, saturating at 0). (read) Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C9878): added to S = Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) 064D64 x Retard Multiplier A (Enriched) 064E78 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding, while the in-Drive idle condition FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant): automatic coding, neutral input clear, pedal released, slow) and afterwards until the in-Drive idle air reduction FFF8B160 has ramped back to its target. Never on a manual car (inferred from that chain). 0x0F2248 (read): when FFF8A7E4 bit 4 is set, B242 = this(coolant) << 6 (12.5 rpm per count) replaces the idle-mode target chain. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 5 is mapped to 6 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (AT state code FFF8A7DD = 0 or 5, 0x0EC7A4; physical meaning not settled). Never on a manual car (read, 0x0F2BCC). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description:
Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only while FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (0x0F38D0, read): automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear) and the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 clear, accelerator released, speed FFF99835 within cals 0x2583F..0x25841, rpm below cal 0x25842 and below @025886(coolant), no speed-sensor/CAN faults; so never on a manual car (read). 0x0EAA40 (read): FFF8B162 = this(coolant) + Idle Air Reduction In Drive (RPM Error)(rpm - target rpm FFF8B236, coolant) + a ramp term (cals 0x25838..0x2583C), >= 0, capped by @025846(coolant); FFF8B160 follows it at cal 0x25834/0x25836 (86) per pass and is subtracted at half weight from the idle air FFF8B200 (0x0F0AF8, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description:
Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant) (automatic coding only). 0x0EAA40 (read): added to the coolant term with the rpm error FFF8CE9C - FFF8B236 (s16, rpm x 5.12) and coolant FFF88A44 as axes. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.
Details: 0x0ECA08 (read; call 0x0ECA88/0x0ECA94 R5 checked): while FFF88A26 bit0 (idle, inferred), engine running (FFF88A27 bit0 clear) and FFF99835 below cal 0x259C8 (255, i.e. always), B1AE = this(new target - ramped target = B236 - B23C/4, capped at cal 0x259CA = 1000 rpm); B1AE enters the idle air at half weight. A positive step (target raised) adds air ahead of the ramp. Used when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear (bit0 = FFF8A7DD in 1..4 or 6, 0x0F38B0). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, AT/CVT Coding)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00DF30. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback).
Details: When used: Only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding (Cal Switches: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT); unused on a manual car (read). LF9F000R: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00DF3C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Trigger A)
table.description: Extra fuel added while the knock torque cap's trigger a trigger is set, by engine speed and load; it fades out afterwards.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Trigger B)
table.description: Extra fuel added while the knock torque cap's trigger b trigger is set, by engine speed and load; it fades out afterwards.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment (Margin)
table.description: Extra fuel added while the knock torque cap's margin trigger is set, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment Decay
table.description: How fast the Trigger A / B knock event enrichment fades once the trigger clears, per pass, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Event Enrichment Ramp (Margin)
table.description: How fast the margin-trigger knock event enrichment moves toward its target and back, per pass, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop)
Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009870. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 009610. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0091B4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A818 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0091C8. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00932C. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. Knock Event Detector: Low Timing
table.description: Watches for ignition timing pulled down to a floor that depends on DAM; when it trips, the knock-event torque limit applies.

table.name: Knock Event Detector: Knocking Cylinders
table.description: Counts cylinders whose knock signal is above the knock threshold while knock correction is already deep; when the count runs up, the knock-event torque limit applies until the learned values are reset.

table.name: Knock Event Latch
table.description: Keeps the knock-event torque limit on after a trip, across key cycles, until the learned knock values are reset.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Passes
table.description: Consecutive passes the timing must stay at or below the floor before the low-timing detector trips.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Hysteresis
table.description: Once the timing is at the floor, it must rise this far above it to count as recovered.

table.name: Knock Event Cylinder Count Limit (Feedback)
table.description: Knocking cylinders, summed while feedback knock correction is at or below its threshold, that trip the detector.

table.name: Knock Event Feedback Correction Threshold
table.description: Knocking cylinders are summed while feedback knock correction is at or below this.

table.name: Knock Event Feedback Correction Hysteresis
table.description: Once summing, feedback knock correction must recover this far above the threshold to stop.

table.name: Knock Event Cylinder Count Limit (Fine Learning)
table.description: Knocking cylinders, summed while fine learning knock correction is at or below its threshold, that trip the detector.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Threshold
table.description: Knocking cylinders are summed while fine learning knock correction is at or below this.

table.name: Knock Event Fine Learning Correction Hysteresis
table.description: Once summing, fine learning knock correction must recover this far above the threshold to stop.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Floor
table.description: Ignition timing floor of the low-timing detector at the lowest DAM factor.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing Floor (DAM Adder)
table.description: Added to the low-timing floor in proportion to Knock Event Low Timing DAM Factor.

table.name: Knock Event Low Timing DAM Factor
table.description: How much of the DAM adder applies, by DAM (128 = all of it).

table.name: Knock Torque Cap: Margin Trigger
table.description: Switches on the margin trigger of the knock torque cap: when the knock margin index falls to Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold, the torque ceiling ramps down to the Margin curve.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap: Coolant Condition Bypass
table.description: With this set, the margin trigger also works below Knock Torque Cap Coolant Minimum (unless an ECU flag blocks it).

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold
table.description: Knock margin index at or below which the margin trigger of the knock torque cap sets, by engine speed and load. Lower values let the engine run with less margin before the cap comes in.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Margin Hysteresis
table.description: Once the margin trigger is set, the threshold is raised by this much, so the margin index must climb clearly above it before the trigger releases.

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Coolant Minimum
table.description: Coolant temperature from which the margin trigger works without the bypass.

table.name: Knock Margin Base
table.description: Starting value of the knock margin index by engine speed and load. The index is this, less intake air temperature 2 in degrees C, plus the spark and A/F terms; the knock torque cap's margin trigger sets when it falls to Knock Torque Cap Margin Threshold. Lower values bring the cap and the margin enrichment in sooner.

table.name: Knock Margin Spark Weight
table.description: How strongly Knock Margin Spark Factor moves the knock margin index, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Margin Spark Factor
table.description: Knock margin term by how far the primary ignition request sits above the ignition timing ceiling; 50 is neutral, lower values take margin away. Scaled by Knock Margin Spark Weight.

table.name: Knock Margin A/F Weight
table.description: How strongly Knock Margin A/F Factor moves the knock margin index, by engine speed and load.

table.name: Knock Margin A/F Factor
table.description: Knock margin term by the measured air/fuel ratio; 50 is neutral and higher values add margin. Scaled by Knock Margin A/F Weight.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0); this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00B07C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00A360. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 8)
table.description:
Knock-detection background step for event slot 1, frequency channel 8.
Details: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 1 (Event 1), knock channel 8 of 8 (index 7 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 7 of cal 0x1B97C is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_7 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C180[7] when FFF8A7C2 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D2, gain curve cal 0x26F6F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D01C by the code that reads it (read). LF9D100e: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D030g: same code as LF9D100e; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D011g: same code as LF9D030g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9D010g: same code as LF9D011g; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 00C078. Confidence: inferred.

Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AF1C > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA6C, read). FFF8AE5E counts 10 ms passes while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 > cal 0x229E6 (0; hysteresis 0x229E8) (0x0BA48C, read). FFF8AE64 counts passes while the pedal-released flag FFF88C64 bit 5 is set and speed <= cal 0x229EC (0; hysteresis 0x229EE) (0x0BA7E0, read); FFF8AF1C counts passes while speed <= cal 0x22A0E (0; hysteresis 0x22A10) (0x0C065C, read). So they are the time stopped (pedal released / any pedal) since the car last moved. FFF88BAA is a byte copied from FFF8CC56 / FFF8CC01 / FFF8CC3B (0x080000 segment); its meaning is not identified, so the axis is raw. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4 with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's fast stage.
Drive mode 4 with manual coding (AT/CVT Coding clear). Step2B of Path B, by gear x rpm (0-4000 rpm), before the Path B gear and pedal factors; looked up into FFF84100..FFF8410E (0x0BBE42..0x0BBF6E). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)).
