table.name: Surge Damping Timing Combustion Mode Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by combustion mode (0 = off, 1.0 = full).

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim Enable
table.description: Switches on the per-cylinder timing trim tables.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description: Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description:
AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear (never on the manual coding), FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D030 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06DE98. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4 with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's fast stage.
Drive mode 4 with manual coding (AT/CVT Coding clear). Step2B of Path B, by gear x rpm (0-4000 rpm), before the Path B gear and pedal factors; looked up into FFF84100..FFF8410E (0x0BBE42..0x0BBF6E). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM
Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description: Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target.

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Event)
table.description: Torque ceiling while the knock-event detector has tripped, by engine speed.

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Margin)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its margin trigger is set and the selector flag is clear, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Margin, Selector)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its margin trigger is set and the selector flag is set, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger A)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its trigger a trigger is set and the selector flag is clear, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger A, Selector)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its trigger a trigger is set and the selector flag is set, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger B)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its trigger b trigger is set and the selector flag is clear, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Maximum Torque (Knock Cap, Trigger B, Selector)
table.description: Torque ceiling of the knock torque cap while its trigger b trigger is set and the selector flag is set, by engine speed (no limit at the top of the scale).

table.name: Knock Torque Cap Ramp Rate
table.description: How fast the margin torque ceiling moves toward its curve, and back up afterwards, per pass, by engine speed.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 Reset MAP
Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 2 Hold MAP
Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description: Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables).

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal)
table.description: The speed limiter in use: the share of the driver's pedal request allowed (100 % = no limit) by vehicle speed. It works above Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Minimum RPM. The other three speed tables are variants for drive mode 3 (Intelligent) and for a VDC flag: to move or remove the limit, edit all four, or turn on Pedal Limits Disable. The fuel-cut Vehicle Speed Limit set is a separate limiter.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), while a status flag from the VDC unit is set (its meaning is not decoded). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Minimum RPM
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: Takes over from the speed tables when the vehicle speed cannot be trusted (a speed sensor fault, or CAN messages from the transmission or VDC missing): the pedal request is then limited by engine speed. Leave it as it is unless you know you need to change it.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit, while the VDC flag is set.

Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut

Idle Air Request to Throttle Area
Idle Air Request to Throttle Area (Monitor)
Throttle Offset Step IAT Factor

table.description: Barometric factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.description: Barometric factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset RPM Threshold (Coolant)
table.description: Engine speed, by coolant temperature, below which a throttle offset ramp acts (probably a cold / low-speed throttle offset).

Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Below Idle Target)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Leave alone.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone unless you know the model.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, Below Idle Target)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Below Idle Target, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed) used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, Below Idle Target, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, TGV Closed) used while rpm is far below the idle target (later software versions).

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description: Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (Alt)
table.description: The live version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter on 2017+ ROMs.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter used while the TGVs are closed. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: The live version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed) on 2017+ ROMs.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric-pressure factor on Spark Air Compensation Limiter (later software versions).

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
Manifold Model Rising Transient Gain Multiplier
table.description: Gain multiplier of the manifold-pressure model during (and one pass after) a rising pressure transient, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the rising-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold
table.description: A falling transient starts when manifold pressure drops this far below its filtered value (negative), in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the falling-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient threshold, in neutral.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient hysteresis, in neutral.

Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)

Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Normally leave alone. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used instead of the other Map A tables while the car is at a standstill under high load (speed 5 km/h or less, pedal 80 % or more, load 40 % or more, for 1 s). Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Standstill High Load)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map B is the steady-state value the estimate settles to, by rpm and load, used while an unidentified speed/pedal/load flag is set. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier A (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) by timing retard. The Map A part only shapes how the estimate moves while conditions change: it is added through Filter A and taken off again through Filter B, so the settled value depends only on Map B x Retard Multiplier B.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (No Enrichment) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Retard Multiplier B (Enriched)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Multiplies Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) by timing retard: more retard, hotter estimate.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter A (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map A part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Rising)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a rising value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Filter B (Falling)
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. How quickly the Map B part of the estimate follows a falling value (higher = faster).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): an amount added to the estimate at the start of each fuel cut, by air quantity, which then decays away by Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Decay
table.description: Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred): how fast the fuel-cut term from Exhaust Temperature Model Fuel Cut Step decays, by air quantity (1.0 = no decay).

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)

A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start

A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (2D)
table.description: Later-software version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C9878): added to S = Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) 064D64 x Retard Multiplier A (Enriched) 064E78 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). LF9F000R: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06AB80. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map B Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80: added to U = Exhaust Temperature Model Map B (Enriched) 064E04 x Retard Multiplier B (Enriched) 064E54 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). LF9F000R: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06AC20. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Enrichment Adder
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to the second exhaust temperature estimate while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred).
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0) and FFF8AE27 bit 4 is clear. 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D8F60 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C965C): added to Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Enriched) 064A0C x Retard Multiplier 064AAC / 256. LF9F000R: a table LF75404S does not have. LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06A878. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. This, not 1B, sets wide-open-throttle intake timing near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle), at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. Near sea level Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. This is the table that sets light-load intake timing on most cars.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the TGV-closed target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to the final intake cam target near sea level (whatever the TGV state; with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees, scaled by the intake coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496BD)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Mid, breakpoint 0x496BE)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp High, breakpoint 0x496BC)
table.description: Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from the fully advanced rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, at altitude (near sea level 1B is used). Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more valve overlap. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Exhaust Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = more overlap. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. Higher = more overlap. High-pedal meaning inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap (internal EGR).

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset A (Altitude)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target at altitude (whatever the TGV state), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Positive = more retard.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2A (High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the TGV-closed target at altitude. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target near sea level, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. It applies whatever the TGV state: with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 2B (High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Extra exhaust cam retard (degrees, scaled by the exhaust coolant factor) added to the high-pedal (near wide-open) TGV-open target at sea level. Not present in the 2015/2016 builds.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3. Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B is added on top of it in all TGV states, so with the TGVs closed both act.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496C5)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Mid, breakpoint 0x496C6)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp High, breakpoint 0x496C4)
table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description: Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure.

Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 024B30 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 02D624. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 024B70 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 02D664. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 037A46 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Address 044B16. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05D4D8 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF9L000E: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06E3FC. Confidence: inferred.

'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85648 = this(lower gear FFF8A8BA); the lower gear is advised (FFF85679 = 1) only if its engine speed FFF8B434 <= FFF85648. 05D5B8 (normal) is 31232 = 6100 rpm for every gear. table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description: Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description: Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description: How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active.

Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 (an early warm-up phase).

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description: Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop)
Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04E960. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description: Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description: Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.

table.name: Additional Enrichment Throttle Threshold
table.description: Throttle opening above idle, by rpm, needed to enable Additional Enrichment A/B.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04E688. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04FDE4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04F1A0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted DAM/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05B560 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04F1B4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 2, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 2 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 2 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 2, Short Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 2 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 2 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 3, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 3 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 3, Short Window)

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (From 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1).
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the AT/CVT curve branch, mirrored by the MT branch that reads Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1); the MT coding flag s4 picks the MT curve). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05B880 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04F4D4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 1.
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the gear-1 branch of the AT/CVT phase-factor lookup). Phase factor (x/255) by the rpm swing count FFF8A75E. With gear FFF88FCE = 0 or above 6 no table is read and the last factor is held (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05B79C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 04F3F0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Combustion Mode Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by combustion mode (0 = off, 1.0 = full).

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim Enable
table.description: Switches on the per-cylinder timing trim tables.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description: Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description:
AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear (never on the manual coding), FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05D030 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050B60. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1)
table.description: Added to Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) by time since the engine started running and coolant, in the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode; manual-car set.

Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 024B30 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 021014. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 024B70 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 021054. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05C6F4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0502B0. Confidence: read.

EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05CAB4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050658. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs closed.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05CADC by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050680. Confidence: inferred.

Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). table.name: EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration
table.description:
How long, by manifold pressure, the EGR tip-out cap is held after a pedal tip-out.
0x0FA068 (read): looked up with FFF8869C (copy of MAP FFF88A34, read) on the rising edge of the tip-out flag; while the flag counter FFF8B2A8 is below it, the target is held at the tip-out limit. p16 (read): EGR module 0x0F94A8 runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C). LV9N000C: located from LF75404S 05CA08 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N002E: same code as LV9N000C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N002I: same code as LV9N002E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0505AC. Confidence: inferred.

table.description: Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
