table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop)
Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05128C. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050FE4. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0527BC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051B58. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted DAM/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05B560 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051B6C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)

For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.description: AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor.

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
table.description: Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input.

table.name: Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim Enable
table.description: Switches on the per-cylinder timing trim tables.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target (AT Drive Range)
table.description: AT version of Closed-Pedal Timing Target, used with the pedal released while the transmission is probably in a drive range.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier

Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AF1C > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA6C, read). FFF8AE5E counts 10 ms passes while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 > cal 0x229E6 (0; hysteresis 0x229E8) (0x0BA48C, read). FFF8AE64 counts passes while the pedal-released flag FFF88C64 bit 5 is set and speed <= cal 0x229EC (0; hysteresis 0x229EE) (0x0BA7E0, read); FFF8AF1C counts passes while speed <= cal 0x22A0E (0; hysteresis 0x22A10) (0x0C065C, read). So they are the time stopped (pedal released / any pedal) since the car last moved. FFF88BAA is a byte copied from FFF8CC56 / FFF8CC01 / FFF8CC3B (0x080000 segment); its meaning is not identified, so the axis is raw. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM
Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description: Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 Reset MAP
Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 2 Hold MAP
Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description: Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables).

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit (AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit Hysteresis (AT/CVT)
table.description: How far below the Park/Neutral RPM Limit the engine has to fall before the cut ends.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal)
table.description: The speed limiter in use: the share of the driver's pedal request allowed (100 % = no limit) by vehicle speed. It works above Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Minimum RPM. The other three speed tables are variants for drive mode 3 (Intelligent) and for a VDC flag: to move or remove the limit, edit all four, or turn on Pedal Limits Disable. The fuel-cut Vehicle Speed Limit set is a separate limiter.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), while a status flag from the VDC unit is set (its meaning is not decoded). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Minimum RPM
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: Takes over from the speed tables when the vehicle speed cannot be trusted (a speed sensor fault, or CAN messages from the transmission or VDC missing): the pedal request is then limited by engine speed. Leave it as it is unless you know you need to change it.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit, while the VDC flag is set.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
External Torque Limit Baro Factor
table.description: Air-density correction (barometric part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.

table.name: External Torque Limit IAT Factor
table.description: Air-density correction (intake temperature part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.

Throttle Offset Step IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Step Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset RPM Threshold (Coolant)
table.description: Engine speed, by coolant temperature, below which a throttle offset ramp acts (probably a cold / low-speed throttle offset).

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)

Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0, TGV Open, EGR)
Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Leave alone.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone unless you know the model.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt, TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt) used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C used while the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description: Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (TGV Closed)
table.description: Version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter used while the TGVs are closed. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
Manifold Model Rising Transient Gain Multiplier
table.description: Gain multiplier of the manifold-pressure model during (and one pass after) a rising pressure transient, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the rising-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold
table.description: A falling transient starts when manifold pressure drops this far below its filtered value (negative), in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the falling-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient threshold, in neutral.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient hysteresis, in neutral.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)
Manifold Model Falling-MAP Initial Duration (TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description: On a hot restart, the A/F sensor exhaust model starts from the pipe temperature stored at engine stop, multiplied by this factor by how much the coolant has dropped since. Normally leave alone.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle), at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. Near sea level Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to Intake Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3 so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Factor 3
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant temperature on Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B, the cold-engine correction for the TGV-closed sea-level intake cam target.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from the fully advanced rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, at altitude (near sea level 1B is used). Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = more overlap. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset A (Altitude)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target at altitude (whatever the TGV state), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Positive = more retard.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGVs closed, sea level), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3. Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B is added on top of it in all TGV states, so with the TGVs closed both act.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor 3
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant temperature on Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B, the cold-engine correction for the TGV-closed sea-level exhaust cam target.

table.name: Intake AVCS Enable Delay After Start
table.description: Intake AVCS closed-loop control waits this long after start, by how long the engine was off and the oil temperature when it stopped.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Enable Delay After Start
table.description: Exhaust AVCS closed-loop control waits this long after start, by how long the engine was off and the oil temperature when it stopped.

Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 4 to 6)
Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 5 to 6)

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 4)

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 8)

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 024AF0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 021DF8. Confidence: read.

Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level (TGV Closed)
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:
Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart, by start type and coolant. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). TGVs not forced closed. Selected instead of the cranking value only inside the engine stop-start restart window (FFF89053 bit3/bit4 with the FFF88ADA bit3 edge, before the decay delay), by start type FFF8A6E8 (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05C5E8 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052BF4. Confidence: read.

EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CAB4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0530C0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs closed.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CADC by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0530E8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
Multi-injection version of the TGV-open EGR tip-out cap.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CAC8 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0530D4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
Multi-injection version of the TGV-closed EGR tip-out cap.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CAF0 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0530FC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration
table.description:
How long, by manifold pressure, the EGR tip-out cap is held after a pedal tip-out.
0x0FA068 (read): looked up with FFF8869C (copy of MAP FFF88A34, read) on the rising edge of the tip-out flag; while the flag counter FFF8B2A8 is below it, the target is held at the tip-out limit. p16 (read): EGR module 0x0F94A8 runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CA08 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 053014. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description: Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05AD10. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05AC90. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05A894. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05A8A8. Confidence: inferred.

table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs not closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Correction to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal), the second pulse; positive = later. Edit with that table.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal pressed or the car moving.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle, Alternate)
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection).

table.name: Purge Valve Duty
table.description: Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.

table.name: Ignition Dwell Time
table.description: Coil charge (dwell) time in milliseconds by rpm and battery voltage, used whenever the engine runs. More dwell gives a stronger spark but heats the coils.

table.name: Timing Request Enrichment Retard
table.description: Retard ramped into the timing request while open-loop power enrichment is active, by load and rpm. The ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and request + knock advance.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0); this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05C240. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05B5DC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (From 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out
table.description: Limits how fast the timing request may climb back to the closed-pedal target just after the pedal is released, by rpm. Lower values give a softer return.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 2)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 2: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1).
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the AT/CVT curve branch, mirrored by the MT branch that reads Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1); the MT coding flag s4 picks the MT curve). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05B880 by the code that reads it (read). LF75500A: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05B910. Confidence: read.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (Gear 1, Below 1800 RPM)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Combustion Mode Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by combustion mode (0 = off, 1.0 = full).

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim Enable
table.description: Switches on the per-cylinder timing trim tables.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description: Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description:
AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear (never on the manual coding), FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). LF75500A: same code as LF75404S; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600H: same code as LF75500A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF75600S: same code as LF75600H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05D0C0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT, Monitor)
Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AF1C > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA6C, read). FFF8AE5E counts 10 ms passes while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 > cal 0x229E6 (0; hysteresis 0x229E8) (0x0BA48C, read). FFF8AE64 counts passes while the pedal-released flag FFF88C64 bit 5 is set and speed <= cal 0x229EC (0; hysteresis 0x229EE) (0x0BA7E0, read); FFF8AF1C counts passes while speed <= cal 0x22A0E (0; hysteresis 0x22A10) (0x0C065C, read). So they are the time stopped (pedal released / any pedal) since the car last moved. FFF88BAA is a byte copied from FFF8CC56 / FFF8CC01 / FFF8CC3B (0x080000 segment); its meaning is not identified, so the axis is raw. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time stopped with the pedal released. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AE64 > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA5C, read; the gate also opens via the two other gate tables).
