table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 024B30 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N300F: same code as LV9N300E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 021E38. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding: mode 7 is mapped to 8 while FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is clear (read, 0x0F2BCC). Never on a manual car. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 8 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 024B70 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N300F: same code as LV9N300E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Data at 021E78. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05C6F4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N300F: same code as LV9N300E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 052D00. Confidence: read.

table.description:

table.description:

EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LV9N301A: located from LF75404S 05CAB4 by the code that reads it (read). LV9N300E: same code as LV9N301A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LV9N300F: same code as LV9N300E; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0530C0. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
How long, by manifold pressure, the EGR tip-out cap is held after a pedal tip-out.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Torque Adder (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Torque Adder (Mode 1) for the manual car.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set. Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32; in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0. Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum (Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description:
Minimum coolant for TGV closing used only while a warm-up fallback flag is set.
TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum, requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay. States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set. Confidence: read.

table.description: Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)

Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050C20. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05090C. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05AF94 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 050F34. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0520C4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05B54C by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051460. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted DAM/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05B560 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 051474. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 4 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 4 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 4)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 4 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 8)
table.description:
Knock-detection background step for event slot 2, frequency channel 8.
Details: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 8 of 8 (index 7 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 7 of cal 0x1B97D is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_7 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C190[7] when FFF8A7C3 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes: +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (3rd Gear / Fault)
Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (From 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum
Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out
table.description: Limits how fast the timing request may climb back to the closed-pedal target just after the pedal is released, by rpm. Lower values give a softer return.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard
Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Closed-Pedal Resume)
Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Pedal Resume)
Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.description: AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor.

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
table.description: Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input.

table.name: Ignition Timing Per-Cylinder Trim Enable
table.description: Switches on the per-cylinder timing trim tables.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target (AT Drive Range)
table.description: AT version of Closed-Pedal Timing Target, used with the pedal released while the transmission is probably in a drive range.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description: Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1)
table.description: Added to Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) by time since the engine started running and coolant, in the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode; manual-car set.

Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set. Gate of Path B: Path B stays available while FFF8AF1C > this(FFF88BAA) (0x0BBA6C, read). FFF8AE5E counts 10 ms passes while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 > cal 0x229E6 (0; hysteresis 0x229E8) (0x0BA48C, read). FFF8AE64 counts passes while the pedal-released flag FFF88C64 bit 5 is set and speed <= cal 0x229EC (0; hysteresis 0x229EE) (0x0BA7E0, read); FFF8AF1C counts passes while speed <= cal 0x22A0E (0; hysteresis 0x22A10) (0x0C065C, read). So they are the time stopped (pedal released / any pedal) since the car last moved. FFF88BAA is a byte copied from FFF8CC56 / FFF8CC01 / FFF8CC3B (0x080000 segment); its meaning is not identified, so the axis is raw. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <=...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >=...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set, FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04, and the Path B gate is open. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM
Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description: Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 Reset MAP
Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 2 Hold MAP
Park/Neutral RPM Limit (AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: with the selector in P or N, cylinders are cut once the engine reaches this speed, so a parked car cannot be revved past it. The cut stays on until the engine drops by the hysteresis. It does nothing on a manual-coded ECU. Separate from the normal rev limit.

table.name: Park/Neutral RPM Limit Hysteresis (AT/CVT)
table.description: How far below the Park/Neutral RPM Limit the engine has to fall before the cut ends.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal)
table.description: The speed limiter in use: the share of the driver's pedal request allowed (100 % = no limit) by vehicle speed. It works above Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Minimum RPM. The other three speed tables are variants for drive mode 3 (Intelligent) and for a VDC flag: to move or remove the limit, edit all four, or turn on Pedal Limits Disable. The fuel-cut Vehicle Speed Limit set is a separate limiter.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal), while a status flag from the VDC unit is set (its meaning is not decoded). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag), in drive mode 3 (Intelligent). Edit it together with the other three.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Minimum RPM
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: Takes over from the speed tables when the vehicle speed cannot be trusted (a speed sensor fault, or CAN messages from the transmission or VDC missing): the pedal request is then limited by engine speed. Leave it as it is unless you know you need to change it.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal, VDC Flag) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit
table.description: As Vehicle Speed Limit (Pedal) Speed Signal Fault RPM Limit, while the VDC flag is set.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
External Torque Limit Baro Factor
table.description: Air-density correction (barometric part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.

table.name: External Torque Limit IAT Factor
table.description: Air-density correction (intake temperature part) applied to a torque limit received over CAN, probably from the transmission controller.

table.name: Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, EGR)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (TGV Open, EGR, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, EGR)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Closed, EGR, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open, Monitor)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open, EGR)
Throttle Opening from Target Torque (Cruise, TGV Open, EGR, Monitor)
Idle Air Request to Throttle Area
Idle Air Request to Throttle Area (Monitor)
Throttle Offset Step IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Step Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit IAT Factor
table.description: Intake-temperature factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset Limit Baro Factor
table.description: Barometric factor on the lower limit of a small throttle offset ramp.

table.name: Throttle Offset RPM Threshold (Coolant)
table.description: Engine speed, by coolant temperature, below which a throttle offset ramp acts (probably a cold / low-speed throttle offset).

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed, EGR)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open, EGR)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0, TGV Closed)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0, TGV Closed, EGR)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0, TGV Open)
Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0, TGV Open, EGR)
Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description: Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Leave alone.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone unless you know the model.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier C (Alt)
table.description: Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier C, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description: Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs open while AVCS is not controlling (start-up, hold or fault), blended in when AVCS drops out. With knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit; the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map.

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
Manifold Model Rising Transient Gain Multiplier
table.description: Gain multiplier of the manifold-pressure model during (and one pass after) a rising pressure transient, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the rising-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold
table.description: A falling transient starts when manifold pressure drops this far below its filtered value (negative), in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis of the falling-transient detection, in gear.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Threshold (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient threshold, in neutral.

table.name: Manifold Model Falling Transient Hysteresis (Neutral)
table.description: As the falling-transient hysteresis, in neutral.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)
Manifold Model Falling-MAP Initial Duration (TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description: On a hot restart, the A/F sensor exhaust model starts from the pipe temperature stored at engine stop, multiplied by this factor by how much the coolant has dropped since. Normally leave alone.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level: above light part throttle, above about 5200 rpm, or cold. Higher = earlier intake timing. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. This, not 1B, sets wide-open-throttle intake timing near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3A (TGV Closed, Altitude)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle), at altitude. Higher = earlier intake timing. Near sea level Intake Cam Target 3B is used instead.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Intake cam advance target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = earlier intake timing. This is the table that sets light-load intake timing on most cars.

table.name: Intake Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Extra intake cam advance (degrees) added to the final intake cam target near sea level (whatever the TGV state; with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Intake Cam Coolant Offset 3B), scaled by Intake Cam Coolant Factor so it can act only when cold. Positive = more advance.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from the fully advanced rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, at altitude (near sea level 1B is used). Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 1B (TGV Open, Normal, Sea Level)
table.description: Main exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more valve overlap. At light part throttle the TGVs close and Exhaust Cam Target 3B is used instead. Normal vs high-pedal split is inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2A (TGV Open, High Pedal, Altitude)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, at altitude. Higher = more overlap. The high-pedal meaning is inferred from the switching conditions.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 2B (TGV Open, High Pedal, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load used when the pedal is near wide open (about 90 % or more), TGVs open, near sea level. Higher = more overlap. High-pedal meaning inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target 3B (TGV Closed, Sea Level)
table.description: Exhaust cam retard target (degrees from rest) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed (light part throttle, cruising) near sea level. Higher = later exhaust closing and more overlap (internal EGR).

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset A (Altitude)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target at altitude (whatever the TGV state), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Positive = more retard.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset B (Sea Level)
table.description: Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target near sea level, scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. It applies whatever the TGV state: with the TGVs closed it adds on top of Exhaust Cam Coolant Offset 3B.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description: Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure.

table.name: Intake AVCS Enable Delay After Start
table.description: Intake AVCS closed-loop control waits this long after start, by how long the engine was off and the oil temperature when it stopped.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Enable Delay After Start
table.description: Exhaust AVCS closed-loop control waits this long after start, by how long the engine was off and the oil temperature when it stopped.

Exhaust AVCS OCV Current Integral Step
Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 4 to 6)
Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 5 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 5 (warm idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 4)
Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.description:
Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.
Transient cap A819 (0x0FA1F8, rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616, read): while the flag is set, the ramped target A817 = min(this, base target) for EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration passes, then ramps back up by cal 0x2D6CE per pass (0x0FA068, read). The flag is set when FFF8AF00 (pedal, per my research notes) is at or below cal 0x2D2A8 and has fallen by at least cal 0x2D2AA against a sample from cal 0x2D2AC passes earlier (read), i.e. a pedal tip-out (inferred). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05CAB4 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182B28 (read, all stack args checked in the assembly) has three sources for the booster vacuum Confidence: read.

table.description:
Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Same data block as descriptor 05D468 (one entry). Road speed per 1000 rpm for gear index 1-8. 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.3 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 6 steps here, 11.0 to 53.9 over 8 in the Alternate table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05D450 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0531CC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM (Alternate)
table.description:
Alternate road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.
Details: When used: used instead of Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Same data block as descriptor 05D474 (one entry). 0x11031C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1175 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, gear FFF8A8BA, speed FFF88BE8, selector FFF8A8C3): only when cal 0x57585 bit 3 is set, FFF8558A = this(gear) (the Alternate table when FFF8A8C3 = 2) and FFF85588 = speed x 28800 / FFF8558A -> FFF8B434. 0x110398 does the same with the second gear index FFF8A8BC (0x1143CC) through the shared descriptors -> FFF8B436. 0x116A0C (gear advice, gated by the same bit) uses B436/B434 as rpm x 0.1953125 to convert the current power to torque at those engine speeds (read). The values (11.0 to 53.9 km/h per 1000 rpm over 8 steps here, 11.3 to 53.9 over 6 in the normal table) do not fit the 6MT, so this belongs to another transmission (inferred). LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05D45C by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0531D8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.
Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05D4D8 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 053254. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Alternate rpm limit, by gear, below which a downshift may be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: instead of 05D5B8 when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read): FFF85648 = this(lower gear FFF8A8BA); the lower gear is advised (FFF85679 = 1) only if its engine speed FFF8B434 <= FFF85648. 05D5B8 (normal) is 31232 = 6100 rpm for every gear. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05D5C4 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 053340. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM
table.description:
Minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.
Details: When used: 05D5E4 replaces it when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Gear advice module 0x116A0C. With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. 0x116A0C (read, lookup by pedal FFF88A5E and upper gear FFF8A8BC): FFF85646 = this; the upper gear is advised only if its engine speed FFF8B436 >= FFF85646. LF75200T: located from LF75404S 05D5D0 by the code that reads it (read). LF75100D: same code as LF75200T; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF73100A: same code as LF75100D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 05334C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description: Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description: Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.

A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1
table.description: Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description: Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never).

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 065AF8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop)
Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is set (read; 2017 0x36B76, 2018 0x37FF2). The bit is the first argument of 0x0CE854 (call in 0x0C589C, read). With it set, 0x0CE854 uses this table + cal 0x18DDC in place of the base table plus the DAM-scaled additive, while DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x18DDD; otherwise Primary Open Loop Fueling + cal 0x18DDC (read). The TGV/AVCS group has its own alternate (Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)); edit both if you enable the switch. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05AC80 by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0618AC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description:
Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.
Details: When used: only with cal 0x2F79A bit 4 set and DAM16 FFF811AE < cal 0x1391C (16). Replaces the TGV/AVCS blend plus knock additive in FFF8A681. 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear. With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05AC00 by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0616A0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05A804 by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 061244. Confidence: inferred.

table.description: Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05A91C by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 0613BC. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05AF94 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05C1B0 by the code that reads it (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 062EBC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05B54C by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 062238. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted DAM/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05B560 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). LF78003A: same code as LF78001H; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LF77000C: same code as LF78003A; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06224C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 4, Channel 3)
table.description: Knock signal processing for event slot 4, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
